utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Dr. Gerxhaliu, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We will continue now with your evidence. Please remember that the solemn declaration which you made at the beginning of your evidence on Monday continues to apply to the evidence you will be giving today. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Dr. Gerxhaliu, today I will just be clarifying a few points in relation to where we left off on Monday. That was when you explained yesterday that Sheribane went to the police to report killings, the killing of 31st of May, 1999. I would like you to try to answer my questions as short as you can, as we don't have so much time today. Now, you mentioned that other crimes had been reported. What was the nature of those crimes? Theft, violence, killings? Could you just very briefly explain what crimes you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was referring mainly to murders committed in the stream of Studime village now and again and also in the course of May, month of May. Let me look at the date briefly. On the 14th of May, six civilians were killed. On the 23rd, nine Albanian girls were killed, and this was the case often but they denied it when they talked about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Gerxhaliu. So you told the police about these crimes. Did the police investigate the crimes? I think you can answer just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The previous ones I referred to, they denied them altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So why on the 31st of May did you report the killings to the police?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did so for them to come and see for themselves the family of Seladin Gerxhaliu whose entire family was executed. And my uncle and his son live a little bit further away, they came afterwards and looked at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And I understand from your statement that the police did respond on the 31st of May. At that time, did the police examine the bodies at the house of the family?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: My father contacted the police, my father's name is Salihu, and some other cousins, but I personally was not there. There was no way I could contact the police. But I know that they came to the scene, took snapshots of the dead bodies that day, and then they told my relatives to wait until they would let them know what to do with the corpses and then they informed them that they could bury them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you see the bodies at the house?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the police went there, some villagers and I carried the bodies to the cemetery. I have the photos of the dead bodies which were taken by my relatives, whereas when we brought bodies to the cemetery, I took photos of them myself. So I saw the bodies, before we took them to the cemetery, and before burying them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you pick the bodies up as they were lying at the house or where did you pick them up?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were all piled up together in one room. Before I couldn't say this because I didn't want to hurt the family members, but in fact, they were all put together in the same room, with the exception of these three persons I mentioned earlier, my uncle and his two sons. So all these bodies, I carried them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is the reference to a room there actually a reference to a grave?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Dr. Gerxhaliu, when you picked up the bodies, did you take them, the bodies, out of the house of the family where they had been killed?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From the house we took the bodies, with the exception of three bodies who were executed one kilometre away from the house, my uncle and his two sons. The others, the old woman, the children and the daughter-in-law, they were all killed inside the house. And as I said, we took their bodies from this house and took them to the cemetery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you look at the list of names in the statement which you have and look at paragraph number 32?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I think we need to supply the witness with a copy of the statement. Maybe we can give a hard copy of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It was to clarify the ones who were not found in the house. Can you do that, Mr. Marcussen?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I think that is described, if I can just look at paragraph 30 in Dr. Gerxhaliu's statement. The three -- yes, there are three persons mentioned in the English version of the statement, paragraph 30, the three persons are Xhemajl, Seladin, and Seladin's son Shaban. And the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, just hold on a second. The reference is to an uncle and two sons, so that wouldn't fit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Dr. Gerxhaliu, the three persons you were referring to, what are their names, please, the three that were killed one kilometre away from the house?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seladin is the owner of the house, the father of six sons and one daughter who were killed. Shaban is the elder son of Seladin, who was only 16. Whereas Xhemajl is my uncle, or the son of Seladin's uncle, who went to save Seladin's life.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So when you referred to three people, just so it's clear on the record, the three people that were executed about a kilometre from the house are Xhemajl, Seladin, and Shaban?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. And then in paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think the remaining nine family members that were killed at the house, they are listed at paragraph 32 of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Dr. Gerxhaliu, just one last point on this. When you picked up the bodies from the house, had the police moved the bodies or did you find them as they -- in the position where they were lying as they had been killed?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police, one investigating judge, and a doctor who had come as a refugee from Croatia, Natalia Tasi was her name - I used to know her from the past - they examined the bodies and moved them a little bit. So before I went there, they had been moved.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: When did -- the team that came to investigate, did they interview and take statements from anyone, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had interviewed my father, Salihu, who was the first to enter the room after having found the three dead persons killed farther from the house. They asked my father about me and my whereabouts, because they knew me. My father lied to them, telling them that I was allegedly in Skopje, in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Dr. Gerxhaliu, did anybody else come to investigate at the crime scene or was there only that one investigation?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only that day, that is on the 31st of May, first it was this team I mentioned that came. I wasn't there, as I said. But they informed me, I was hiding somewhere else, and then there was a team that came just to inform the people that they could bury the bodies. I don't know if any other investigation having taken place. I heard, though, that on the 6th of June another team came, a combined team, and they went to the site of the crime and to the other place where the three people had been killed, as I explained, and then there was this clash with the KLA that was the second time but mainly they picked up the cartridges or some other materials of interest to them, and as I was informed, fighting took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: To your knowledge, Dr. Gerxhaliu, have anybody ever been tried for the crimes -- for the killing of the 12 people we talked about?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never heard that anyone was found responsible but not -- not in this case, for the family I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Dr. Gerxhaliu, the team which came on the 6th of June, do you understand that to have been an investigating team?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I may only tell you what I heard, namely that there were police representatives as well as army representatives in this team, going there, as I was told, to investigate. But it was my cousin Fatbardha who saw them, her mother and another cousin whom they -- this team took to show them where the event had taken place. This is the only thing I can tell you after I heard this from them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is it your understanding that the KLA prevented them carrying out an investigation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. But as the people I mentioned earlier informed me, they passed the neutral line, they went a little bit further than where the victims were, and by accident they ran into KLA forces and a fighting ensued. This was the reason why, because they passed that line, and ran into KLA at the barn, as we say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution have no further questions at this point to the witness. We might of course do some redirect, but now we are finished. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we'll proceed in this order: General Ojdanic, General Pavkovic, Mr. Sainovic, Mr. Milutinovic, Mr. Lazarevic and General Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Dr. Gerxhaliu. My name is Tomislav Visnjic, attorney-at-law, and counsel for General Ojdanic. I have a few questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: One thing I forgot, before you start, excuse me. Doctor, you mentioned photographs. Do you have these photographs with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And some were taken by relatives and some were taken by you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't receive any translation. The photographs of family members of Seladin were taken by my cousin, Fatbardha, together with another cousin, Sela, in the house while the other photographs were taken at the cemetery. We took them together. I've brought the film here, and I also have the pictures here with me. I have brought the film here at the Tribunal earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What was -- what was the date on which you took your photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the same day, before they were buried; that is, on the 31st of May. Some of the photographs were taken at 11.00 while the others around 3.00 before the bodies were buried. So in one word, all the photographs were taken on the same day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Just give us a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Dr. Gerxhaliu, would you like us to look at these photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I would appreciate that. I have them here. Maybe the Tribunal has the film or the photographs. As you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would the usher please collect them from Dr. Gerxhaliu, please. Doctor, each of these photographs has a number on the back and it would appear initials. Can you explain how these came to be there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't marked them with numbers. I don't know who did that. But I can recognise all the persons on the photographs. They are all cousins of mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I think I can assist with the initials. Those -- there are numbers and I believe some initials on the back of each photograph. Dr. Gerxhaliu provided these photographs to the Office of the Prosecutor in 2002, and I believe these are copies he received back with markings on them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You were not intending to submit the photographs?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: That's correct. And yesterday we informed the Defence that Dr. Gerxhaliu had given us these photographs in 2002, and this morning only have we provided the Defence with copies of the photographs, just to clarify the situation with those. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, Mr. Visnjic, I may be asking too much of you when I ask for confirmation on behalf of everyone, but is it accepted that this family were massacred? Or is there some issue over that?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can only speak for my Defence team. Based on the results of our own investigation, it is obvious that a crime of murder was carried out at that place and several people were murdered. Apart from that, I can't say anymore. But indeed, several people were murdered. That's as far as I can go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does that extend to the three who were not in the house?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would have to count them, but most likely. I don't know how I can confirm this right away. What I can tell you, though, is that we don't have any proper documents. We have some results of our own investigation which we wanted to use in this cross-examination. We don't have the complete set of documents, and you will learn what our findings were. There were some authorities there carrying out an on-site investigation but I don't have all the documents, therefore I can't provide a full answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's just that if there is no real dispute but that these people were murdered, then the clarification of exactly who is shown in the photographs can be dealt with out of court. It doesn't need to be dealt with here and take up time. And all I'm trying to establish is whether there is any issue over the fact of murder. I appreciate there will be an issue over responsibility for the murder, but the fact of murder I was anxious to clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct. Although I think there is a mention of nine people being murdered in the documents. I don't know how many photographs you received from Dr. Gerxhaliu. Perhaps this is something we can clarify at a later stage with the OTP at a later stage of the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Doctor, thank you for giving us these photographs. If you do not mind, we shall hold on to them for the moment, but it may be that the matter can be clarified in the course of the day and the photographs returned to you. We shall see. But we are grateful to have them at the moment. Thank you. And now Mr. Visnjic will carry on with his questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. You can hold them as long as you wish. I brought them there for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gerxhaliu.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 3D65 shown to the witness? 3D65. I don't think this is it. It should be a map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I just want to point out that we, the Prosecution, has not been notified of any documents that the Defence would use. I would not object to Mr. Visnjic showing the map but I just thought I should point that out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe this was disclosed three days ago, and they are in the system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think the point that's being made is that you should give a list of the documents you propose to use in the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I agree it may have been our omission, but I hope that during our cross-examination we will be able to realise that the OTP has been notified sufficiently in advance about our intention to use these.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Carry on then for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Could we please have 3D65 shown to the witness? Yes, exactly. Doctor, this is a map of a part of the Vucitrn municipality. As opposed to the one you saw yesterday, this one is a bit lighter. I would kindly ask you to show the border or the line between the KLA and the Serb positions before the outbreak of the war between the 20th and the 24th of March, 1999. I have in mind the part towards the territory of Sudimlja and Slakovce, and that's the operational zone called Llap, I think. You don't need to point out where Salju [phoen] is and the rest.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the Llap operational zone is concerned, it was operational in Podujeve. I don't know where its border line was. And secondly, I was a doctor and I was mainly active in logistics. In other words, I was active in hospitals. So I'm not a person who can answer your questions about the Llap operational zone. It was a totally different zone. But for Shala zone, I have already pointed it out in the map, where the border line was.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Now, if it's not a problem for you, could you please draw the line again between Shala and the Serb forces in your own municipality, please? Before the beginning of the war, between the 20th and the 24th, please.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I am a doctor, I'm not expert in maps, but since you insist, I will try to show you approximately where this line was. This is Studime e Poshteme. This is Studime e Eperme. This is Sllakovc. And this is Samadrexha. The Serb forces were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Hold on, doctor, that doesn't help us for reasons which are no fault of yours. Is this -- are you looking for the same line as was drawn on a map yesterday? On Monday, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm just asking him to show me one of those lines. He showed seven yesterday. I just need one and then I'm going to put further questions about that. It is the same line but it's one of seven, one of the seven that were there. I think that this map is more precise in view of the question that I wish to put to the witness. That is the simple reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we want to be sure we are getting the same reflection of evidence, don't we? You can't use the other map? You've got to use this one, have you?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I think it's going to create a great deal of confusion and I'm just interested in one locality. Once he draws the line, I have a question for that particular locality and then we can move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you not simply ask him what side of the line that locality was on, or is it a more complex question than that?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, all right. I guess, well, yes, I guess we can do it that way, too, and then we can show him that map, the map from Monday, that is. But this is how I shall proceed now.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gerxhaliu, please tell me, did the KLA -- actually, let's start this way. You said in your statement that the KLA held 80 per cent of the territory in Vucitrn; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me if I tell you that what you marked on the map [Overlapping microphones] is considerably less than 80 per cent of the territory of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was my estimate because it included Cicavica with all the villages, and then Studime e Eperme, and the villages around this village. So this was my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: All right. I agree. Now that you said Sudimlja, what about Svracak, Donji and Gornji, were they under KLA control before the war broke out in 1999?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean Sfaracak, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both Sfaracaks were under the control of the former Yugoslav forces. They were positioned in upper Sfaracak. There there is a strategic hill, while in Studime e Poshteme they were positioned in the Rashica neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: All right. From when did they have these positions in Gornji Svracak?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sfaracak i Poshtem, later on, but in Sfaracak i Eperm, and in Studime, somewhere in March. I don't know the exact time, but I can say that they held these positions under their control throughout the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Why did you then state in your statement in paragraph 6 that Svracak was under the control of the Serb forces from the end of April?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, whether it was April or March, I can't tell you. I have mentioned things in my statement only briefly. I don't think it's important now whether they were there in March or April. The most important thing is that the forces were -- the former Yugoslav forces were positioned from March onwards on both hills, on both these positions. If you want the precise dates, I have a notebook in my house, and there you can find the details, while in my statement I only pointed out things briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic, where is that in the statement? In paragraph 6?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, paragraph 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: From the -- yes, sorry, I found it. I've found it now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: In actual fact, you don't know whether it was March or April, or what you said in your statement is simply not correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Counsel, listen, I just want to point out one thing. In Sfaracak e Eperm, there were Serb inhabitants, and this area was always under the control of Serb Yugoslav authorities. As for the date when the Serb forces came there and positioned themselves there, I don't know. But I can tell you that that area was under their control. They could position themselves there whenever they wanted to, because that area was simply under their control. And as I said, I don't know the exact dates when they came there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Are you telling me now that this area was never under KLA control and that the KLA never operated in the area?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: The area of Svracak, Gornji and Donji?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't speak of something that I don't know. I know one thing. You can see Sfaracak i Eperm from my house. I had patients there, so I moved to that area often, and I know that there were movements of Serb forces there. And the other Sfaracak is behind a hill, and I cannot see it from my house. I can only confirm things that I've seen with my own eyes. Sfaracak i Eperm, Studime e Poshteme, these two locations were always under the control of the former Yugoslav authorities, until the NATO forces entered Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: All right, doctor. Tell me -- actually, let's move on. In the Milosevic case, you made several references in the transcript to the fact that you treated Albanians and Serbs equally. The transcript pages are 4111 and 4112. When Milosevic asked you whether you knew of the killing and wounding of Albanians by the KLA, your answer was that that was quite inaccurate. I'm asking you now whether you still claim that the KLA never wounded or killed any Albanians.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I haven't heard, and I haven't seen a case when KLA wounded or killed an Albanian. At that time, during that trial, I emphasised that I was working in the hospital and I administered help to anyone who required it. Therefore, as for your question, I cannot confirm something that I haven't seen or heard of.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Doctor, I'm just telling you that in the Milosevic transcript, on page 4119, you didn't say that you don't know. You said that that was untrue.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot confirm something that I don't know. I cannot say somebody killed someone when I haven't seen that. And for me, that is untrue.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: All right. We understand the difference. We understand now what it is that you say is incorrect. In the same case, on page 4117, you said that the police at check-points beat up and mistreated the inhabitants of the villages that were under KLA control. I'm asking you now whether you knew whether somebody was mistreated or beaten by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: At check-points, you mean? Serb police check-points?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I mean the territory that was held by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the territory held by the KLA, I have not witnessed any maltreatment or beating up by KLA soldiers. While in Dakovce, situated on the road towards Pristina, from the side of Vucitrn, there there was a Serb police check-point, it resembled a border post, and everybody was beaten up there, especially those villagers who lived in areas controlled by the KLA. And I have treated many of these persons who were beaten up on this check-point, and they have consequences to this date.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: All right. May the witness please be shown 3D61?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'm not going to repeat my point about not having received the list, but I was going to ask my learned colleague whether there it was an English translation of the document available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, there apparently isn't one at the moment. I'm told there isn't one in the system. Is there? Have you found it? I'm told, Mr. Visnjic, that there is no English version of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There must be a mistake on our part. There would have to be an English version of the document because it's a document from the OTP and I know that I found it in their database. I'm sure that I saw it. I don't know what happened to the translation, but anyway, let it be my problem. Let me ask the witness something about this document actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just hold on. This is the second document to which the same point is made by Mr. Marcussen that by agreement of everyone, the rule was made that a list of the documents or other material that's going to be used in cross-examination should be disclosed when the witness begins his evidence. Now, in this case that would have been on Monday. And that enables obviously the Prosecution to check the position and prepare themselves, and it could avoid this sort of problem. So there are two separate issues here. There is one releasing the documents themselves into the system; but separately there is the question of providing a list of these documents, each time, for each witness. Now, that appears not to have been done here, Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, agree but as far as disclosure, these documents were made available through the system Friday afternoon. So -- well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's not the point. The point is the orderly conduct of the proceedings is assisted by the production of the list. So while it may not be a major infraction of the rules, it nevertheless is something that should be complied with. So, please, in future, and this applies to everyone, and it applies to the Prosecution when they come to cross-examine your witnesses in due course, please ensure that when the witness begins his evidence, that list is always released to the Prosecution. Now, let's carry on using what we do have here, so far as possible. Yes, Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, our very effective case manager has managed to locate a draft translation of the document. I propose we can e-mail that to Defence counsel and to the Bench, and then maybe it will be possible to consult the translation of the document for everyone in the courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we can also proceed with the version which is on the screen, can we not?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to express my gratitude. But Your Honour, I would really like to say that it wasn't our intention to make the work of the OTP any more difficult. As a matter of fact, I think we facilitated their work through our disclosure. But don't worry, we are going to correct it every other time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Doctor --

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Let us proceed. I would like to draw your attention to paragraph 8 of this document, which is a regular operations report in Pristina. We cannot see it on the transcript any longer. At any rate, in paragraph 8, what is mentioned is that on the 24th of September, 1998, in the afternoon, a group of three Siptars from Samodreza, as representatives of the village, took a tractor on their way to the terrorists that were in the immediate vicinity of the village of Cecelija in order to convince them to stop with attacks and to hand over their weapons.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the question because Mr. Visnjic is moving too fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic, in your anxiety to be even more helpful you're moving too quickly for the interpreter, I'm afraid. So the question has been missed. The lead-up to it has been translated but not the question.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We do not have the document in English, so it's a sight translation of B/C/S that was on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Cecelija was under the control of the KLA; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Tell me, the village of Samodreza, was that under KLA control too?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Half of this village, the Basholl neighbourhood was under KLA control, while the lower half of the village was under the control of former Yugoslav forces. They had positions on a hill. They call it the Llazoviq neighbourhood. This was where the Serb forces were positioned and there were clashes on that area every now and then. After 2nd of May, the Serb forces advanced and came to Basholl neighbourhood and they stopped there. They couldn't advance any further. So up to the 2nd of May, they were in Llazoviq neighbourhood of Samadrexha, and after this date, they came to -- 2nd May, 1999.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: If the counsel can wait for the witness to finish his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I'm asking about October. I'm asking you about October and September 1998. So the question is just whether it's Cecelija -- or, rather, Samodreza was under KLA control in September and October 1998. That is the time when you went to these villages and when you treated the wounded.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you want a proper explanation, here it is. I often went to Novoselle of Maxhun and in Samadrexha by my official ambulance vehicle, and up to Samadrexha, which was under the control of the forces that I explained. As for Ceceli it was always under KLA control.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, doctor. Did you hear that the KLA in Cecelija physically mistreated, beat up, and -- some people, and broke a tractor? The persons involved were three Siptars from the village of Samodreza who were representatives of the village and who went out there to talk to the representatives of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Counsel, this is the first time I hear of this incident, and since I have taken the solemn declaration, I cannot confirm this.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Doctor, when you moved about these villages, did you see that the population was moving? Or, rather, that they were moving out, one side or the other?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: For which period of time are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: The period between October and March. October 1998 and March 1999, before the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm anything. I have spoken of things that I know in my statement, and now, during my testimony. Maybe there were people moving out but I don't know that. I have spoken of the movements of my family in my statement. As for others, they might have moved out but seven years have passed and I cannot either confirm or deny anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: All right, doctor. But if I show you document 3D62 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't even dare ask. I hope there is a translation into English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Out of luck again, Mr. Visnjic, I'm afraid. But we are managing with the interpreters doing a sterling job by translating from the screen. The only thing is you need to move just a little bit more slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Well, doctor, it is a list which constitutes a list of villages from which inhabitants were expelled, first Serbs and Montenegrins by the KLA. And as you can see, there are some villages here that you had toured yourself; for example, Gornji Svracak. You went through there, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had patients there but this was before the war. These were Serbs, these patients, and I went to visit them very often.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: We are precisely talking about the period between October and March. October 1998 and March 1999. Can the usher please bring the table back a bit? Can I see the upper part -- or, rather, can the witness see the upper part? Thank you, this will do. What about the other villages, Dolak, Donji Stanovci, Mijalic [phoen], Taradza, did you visit any of them?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Except for upper Sfaracak, which was close to my house, and where I had patients.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the family name of --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Can we see the lower part of the table now, please? Just a little bit further up, please, if possible. Thank you. Now, doctor, are you familiar with any of the villages here on this list? Did you visit any of these?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: During this period, you mean? Or during the war?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I meant the period between October 1998 and March 1999.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Except for upper Sfaracak. There was an older man, 90 years old, who was sick and he was my patient, so I frequently went there to visit him.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Did you not go to Samodreza perhaps?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did go to Samadrexha, but I couldn't go there through the check-point. I usually went through Sfaracak village to Samadrexha.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: That means that you went through territory that was not under control -- under the control of the Serb police, right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I usually went through that road that I mentioned, and not through the road where the check-point was, because I didn't dare.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: So you went through Svarcak because there were no check-points there, right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to Sfaracak and came back, usually through Studime e Eperme, between Ceceli and Samadrexha, and from a road between these two villages I would return back home.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, you've given us a good answer. I'm asking you now, when you were in Samodreza did you notice that the population was moving out? Serbs and Montenegrins, 20 households in the period between the 27th of October, 1998, until March, 1999. Did you notice that?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wasn't there during that time. I haven't seen that. I don't know when they left and what happened to them. I absolutely know nothing. I had no chance to see them move out.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Could we just move the list a bit further down, please. Did you visit any of these villages mentioned here: Milivoda, Strova, Bencuk, Bivoljak, Glavotina, Mijalic, Drvare, Shalce, and Kolo?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: None of the villages you mentioned. I didn't have an opportunity to visit any of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Can we please see the second page of this document. Doctor, on page 2 there is another list of villages. Are you familiar with any of these?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: For example, Cecelija; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: We call it Ceceli. Here it is Cecelija. But it's not a problem at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Well, did you notice that in Cecelija, or Cicilija, or in Slakovce that also some houses were abandoned? Did you notice that?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The movement of the population differed. What I remember, since you insist, during the offensive of September 1998, there were houses abandoned in Ceceli and Sllakovc but to my recollection, the people who had moved out returned to their houses. This was during the offensive, the September offensive, 1998, around 5th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: No, doctor. I'm asking you for the 27th of October, 1998 and until the 15th of March, 1999, as it is stated in this document. I am asking you this because in that territory, the KLA was active, and due to their activities, people were displaced. Do you agree with me if I say that?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot agree with you. I can only say that on the 15th of September, 1998, a Serb offensive was launched and that prior to that the people of Shala e Bajgore, Ceceli, and Samadrexha all went out of their homes, and then they returned, but I cannot ascertain the time of the return or the share of population that returned. I am not competent to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Doctor, between the 27th of October, 1998, until the 15th of March, 1999, why would 220 people move out of Serbian and Montenegrin origins from five villages and 93 Roma from three villages? And on page 1 I believe we see the figure from the five villages which have been completely ethnically cleansed and three being partially ethnically cleansed of the Roma. If that -- if the territory was not under the control of the KLA, why would have these people moved out?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I think the witness has said that he don't know, and I think now he's being asked to speculate about the reasons why they moved out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I suspect also the question has been either -- it looks as though it's been wrongly translated. Did you mean to say, Mr. Visnjic, if the territory was not under control of the KLA why would these people have moved out?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to say, Your Honour, that in the territory where the KLA was active, that there were Serbs and Roma and Albanians who were moved out, as it was stated in the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Doctor, do you know anything of the movement of people in these villages or from these villages between October and March?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I already said, and I will firmly declare, that I know only the movement of the people who were obliged to leave their homes due to the Serb offensive launched on the 15th of September. That was obvious for all of us to see. I cannot say that there were no other moves. There were. But I was not a witness to that so I cannot confirm it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: But doctor --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: On you go, formulate another question. Sorry, Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether I understood my colleague Mr. Visnjic correctly, but according to the translation that I have of the document, the last paragraph that I believe Mr. Visnjic is referring to is not saying that the villages from which the 220 persons were driven out and so on and so forth were in KLA-held area. I think it's a conclusion of the report and doesn't -- which doesn't make that distinction. It's a little complex when we don't have a translation and no time to look at it before. I just wanted to point that out and we can maybe clarify that later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Formulate your next question, please, Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. In the meantime we received the translation in hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Doctor, could we please show a Defence Exhibit to the witness? This is 3D66.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before this new document is being shown to the witness and you've just been provided with a translation of 3D62, this is an official document by the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia, number 350/39, dated the 15th of March 1999. In this document, containing a list of villages where there was recorded movement of population, and the ethnic makeup is provided as well. Also, we see the reasons for the movement of the population stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Doctor, we have another map now, which is a blown-up map. I'm interested in the area between Gornja and Donja Sudimlja, the area you're very familiar with. The reason why I'm using this map is because we see the brook you mentioned on several occasions marked in blue, the brook between Gornja and Donja Sudimlja. It actually follows the road to a great extent. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Can you mark on this map the place where your tractor was the night between the 2nd and the 3rd of May?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I marked it on the other map. I don't know why you should repeat it. Do you have the other map? Of course, if it's necessary, I can do that again. But I know I marked it once.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Please indulge me, I'll ask you for another two locations which are not on the map and perhaps that will clarify.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The convoy was from here, Studime e Eperme, until the entrance to Studime e Poshteme. There is a hill somewhere here. I'm not very good at cartography.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark the spot where your tractor was?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second half of the column, the column was very long from -- in the place between the two Studimes. If we divide it into part, in the second part, in the rear.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Very well. In your village, is there a place called, and I beg your forgiveness for possibly mispronouncing it, but something along the line of Mahala Zusi or something similar?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our villagers live in that neighbourhood and the last name was Zhushi.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Can you mark off that part, approximately, where your neighbours lived?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Studime is only one point. All the neighbourhood comprised Studime. We all lived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: So when we say Mahala Zusi, that would actually be Donji Studime or is it Gornji Studime?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not a Mahalla or a neighbourhood. It's only a group of families, three, four families, who together with my family, Gerxhaliu, live in that part of Studime. That is Studime e Poshteme, or lower Studime.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: It is a part of Donja Sudimlja but closer to or towards Gornji Studime; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In the direction of upper Studime, there is Rashica neighbourhood, whereas we, as I mentioned, we lived together, my family and Zhusi family.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Where would it be on the map, doctor? Is this too small for you to show it?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, understand me, this is only a point. We lived together, Gerxhaliu and Zhushis together.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you this, something called Mahala, the village of Sfaracak or Mahalla Sfaracak. Excuse me, Mahalla Sfaracak or the village of Sfaracak that would probably be Sfaracak. There is no other location with a similar name in that territory, am I correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just to make an explanation, in the lower neighbourhood of the village near the brook live Zhushi and Gerxhaliu but there are also some Krasniqis. In Rashica, most of them in the upper Mahalla or neighbourhood, there are their neighbours. Their last name is Svarcali, Svarcali. It's not the name of the place. It's their last -- their family name.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So that is also a part of Donja Sudimlja?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There is upper neighbourhood where the Svarcali but mostly there are people who moved and then there is our neighbourhood that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to tender this document. I just wanted to say that the red line across the road between Gornja and Donja Sudimlja is the place for which the witness stated his tractor was in the column and the red dot in Donja Sudimlja is the approximate location of his house, and the house of the Zusi family.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit IC 23.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for your reference this map, IC 23, is linked to IC 21, from page 2453 of the transcript of this proceedings, from Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Doctor, on the 3rd of May, you returned to the area between Gornji and Donja [Realtime transcript read in error, "Gornja"] Sudimlja. And bodies were collected, identified and later on buried. My question is this: Did the KLA immediately take over the area above the village of Gornja Sudimlja?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the morning of the 3rd of May, when I went there, it was a bit later, they had taken positions in the upper Studime, that is the KLA soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic, the question there has been translated as returning to the area between Gornji and Gornja Sudimlja, and I think you said Donja and Gornja Sudimlja; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour. I didn't follow the transcript. You are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: The question is, therefore, did the KLA take the area between the villages of Gornja and Donja Sudimlja?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The answer is clear. The witness understood the question okay. I was just making sure the transcript on this was clear because it seems to be of some importance that we identify these locations correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show 3D70 to the witness? It is an official note by the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia dated the 3rd of July 2001. If this document hasn't been given a number, I wanted to say that we do have it in the system, we have it here, I can see it now, and we have the translation just underneath. Your Honour, this document is a document given to our Defence immediately prior to the proceedings as part of a disclosure process by the government of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Doctor, a few moments ago you talked about the reaction of the Serb forces as regards the reported murders. I wanted to ask you this: Did you know that on the 3rd of May 1999, the police station in Vucitrn attempted to carry out an on-site investigation to see what had happened in the area between Gornja and Donja Sudimlja and that they were attacked by the KLA? You were there at the time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can that relate to the same incident? Because I thought we were talking about the 31st of May for the other incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. What is discussed here is the 2nd and the 3rd of May. The big incident when the column was stopped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, I misunderstood your question. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My mistake. I failed to mention the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Doctor, did you know that the Serb police tried on the 3rd of May to carry out an on-site investigation and that they were attacked by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know this, and I never heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Did you know that they were opened fire at from the exact locations you said were Mahala Zusi where your house was and the house of that other family?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time for me to hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that as of the 3rd of May onwards, the KLA controlled that territory up until the end of the war? I have in mine the territory above Gornja Sudimlja.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was control until Studime e Eperme but until that point, not beyond that point, because Serbian forces with tanks and various arms were deployed in that area and there was no chance for KLA to go there until NATO entered. Sfaracak and Studime e Poshteme was in the hands of the Serbian forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Yes. So how could it be, then, that the police were attacked twice in close proximity to your house on the 3rd of May 1999 and during the second on-site investigation, on the 5th of June, on the 5th of June 1999, if that territory was under the police control?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I already said, the 5th, about the 5th or the 6th of June, about that event, I mean, I heard from other people the wife of my uncle was there, the car of the Serbian police, and she told the police about the positions of the KLA, but I didn't see it myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I apologise but I need to interrupt you, doctor. You've already said that. I wanted to ask you this: If the Serb police indeed controlled that, as you assert, what is the explanation for them being attacked twice by the KLA close to your house? Do you have an explanation?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the vicinity of my home, the Serbian police never came. I never saw them come that near and I never heard people say that, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let me ask you this: Did the KLA come close to your house?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already stated in my statement that KLA members often came in their cars in the evening, when I went to check them before I finished my work, but afterwards, I was there in the logistics place --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: No, doctor. We are talking about the period of the war, May 1999. I'm asking you this: In May 1999, was the KLA coming close to your house?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not at home, therefore I cannot say anything. But I know that in Sfaracak i Eperm and Rashica, in these two hills there were forces of the former Yugoslav army, and I believe it was not possible for the KLA to take that part under control because it was being controlled by the Serbian forces, by the Yugoslav forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Your brother, Seladin, wasn't he a member of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: He assisted the KLA, but I'm not sure that he was a member. I know that he helped it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Was he helping them from the start?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot speak for him. I can only speak for myself. I only know that he supplied them with foodstuffs, medicaments, when he had possibility to do that, but I don't think he was ever armed or ever in uniform. I never saw him wearing any uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I will try to jog your memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show D71, I believe, to the witness? We have it in hard copy, and it is not in the system.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, you're looking in my direction. I can confirm that I received a copy just before court started so we do have a copy of it. But otherwise it's the situation as with the other documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We will turn to the document when we come back after the break, Mr. Visnjic. And we'll be back at five minutes past 4.00. One other matter, sorry, at this break and the next one, can parties try to sort out the position about identifying the victims of the 31st of May and whether we need these photographs? It's been helpful to see them, but do we need to retain them or can we deal with that matter in some other way? All right? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before I proceed, may I inform you that I talked to Mr. Marcussen during the break, and together we agreed that it is 12 bodies of persons who had been killed and that on our part, as far as the circumstances are concerned, as to how they -- the persons were killed and so on, the Defence could not accept for the time being what the witness has been saying, but in our own investigation we will try to obtain original documents from the on-site investigation which obviously had been carried out by the investigation authorities of the Republic of Serbia at the time. So, in my opinion, there is no need to keep the photographs. The number of persons involved is not being challenged. We've just agreed that it was nine plus three, and I believe that that will do for the time being. And of course that they had been murdered, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Doctor, I will return these photographs to you. We know that the Office of the Prosecutor has copies if they turn out for any reason to be necessary. But it looks as though there is no dispute about the fact that 12 people were murdered on this occasion. It was useful to us, as I said to you earlier, to see these photographs, but we do not need to keep them from you. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, also while the doctor is having a look at the document that has just been provided to him, before we have this off our screens, the official note, that is, let me just say that this Defence document also has to do with 2465, page 2465 of Monday's transcript when the witness spoke about reporting crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Now, doctor, I would like to continue with your examination. You looked at the document that is before you carefully. Now my question is: Is it correct that your brother Seladin provided the KLA with weapons and later on became a fighter in the 142nd Brigade or, rather, 141st Brigade of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said earlier that I was a doctor, I was part of the logistics, and I was working in the hospital. Seladin, I was informed that he helped the KLA with food supplies and so on, but as I'm under solemn oath I cannot confirm what you are saying. I'm not excluding the possibility that he was a member but, however, I have never seen him with a weapon or in a uniform. It happened during this time that I could not see even my own children for two or three weeks, let alone Seladin and from the picture here, you can see that he's in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: All right, doctor. How many soldiers did the KLA have? How many of them did you treat, rather?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. As I have stated in my statement, I had three rooms in the hospital. One was for wounded whoever they were, civilians or soldiers, and the other two were for women and children. I would say that 70 to 80 per cent of the patients were civilians. As for fighters, they were in less numbers. I cannot claim with certainty how many wounded soldiers from the KLA there were. I can only speak of these things from my professional point of view.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: You are telling me now that actually you cannot say how many soldiers the KLA had, and you were their doctor; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was a doctor of the entire population and the KLA, and I had no reason to know or to show interest in this issue, even to this date. I was highly professional and I had a lot of work to do in connection with my profession at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: All right, doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown Defence Exhibit 3D63.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Doctor, this is yet another report of the MUP of Serbia, 498/99, the date is the 5th of June 1999, and what is claimed in this report is that the military police and the military investigation organs, together with a MUP patrol that went along by way of security, they went to the village of Donja Sudimlja on the 5th of June 1999 in order to carry out an on-site investigation. They were attacked by Siptar terrorist gangs, and in the process, one vehicle was damaged, another vehicle was left where it was, and one person was wounded and also an automatic rifle remained on the spot, and a pistol. It is also stated that, inter alia, they were attacked with a hand-held rocket launcher. Doctor, did you see this document before?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have never seen it. That is, this document. I haven't heard and I haven't seen any evidence that there was a clash with KLA in the vicinity of Seladin's house, because this house is very close to mine. On that day, I left for Ulqin I heard that the fighting took place in the upper part of the village, near a stream. I cannot exclude this possibility, but I can neither confirm it. I would like to know more details about this - names, family names - as I have given you details. You say that on the 24th of September, three Albanians were beaten up and they were in a tractor but you're not mentioning the names of these Albanians. Therefore, I cannot argue if it is a fact or not. I heard that on that day --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Doctor, until today, you have made several statements, and how come you never stated this particular event? How come that you mention it today that this attack took place?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I have spoken of things but you have to make a clear line between things that I have seen myself and things that I've heard. I heard that this took place, and it occurred in the neutral zone above the Rashica neighbourhood, near the stream. I heard this from my co-villagers, from my father, from the wife of my uncle, and I heard about this after I returned from Ulqin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: May I have clarification of one thing? It must be my fault, but the Seladin who is referred to in the exhibit which you were going to put to the witness but didn't, is that the same person as is referred to in paragraph 30 of the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour. It's the same person. And again I would like to show this exhibit to the witness. I just need to deal with these two first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Hear me out, though. Does it say in the statement that he was the brother of the accused -- sorry, brother of the witness? If Mr. Marcussen can help me, I would be grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I do not think so. I'm also trying to verify that at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Why -- it's only now I'm realising the relationship between these two, in spite of having read this several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe at paragraph 27, it says, "That evening I recall sitting on the balcony drinking tea with my cousin Seladin Gerxhaliu."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But we now learn this is the brother, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I take it -- that seems to be -- the witness hasn't said anything to the contrary but he hasn't been asked about that specifically. We could just clarify that with him, maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gerxhaliu, Seladin, is he your brother or your cousin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I actually asked for clarification about the 24th and the 28th. Seladin was a cousin of mine. His father and my grandfather were brothers. So he's only a cousin to me and a neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, if Mr. Marcussen is going to be doing re-direct, I would object at this point. It's improper for him to be doing re-direct examination --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Oh, sit down, we're just trying to get something clarified, for goodness' sake. You don't -- why do you always have to think you're in some American court when you come here? Don't you think we are trying our best to control the proceedings and understand what's going on? Now, Mr. Visnjic. My reason for interrupting was that the witness has so far made it very clear, as I understood it, that this was the brother, in answer to your questions, and now I understand it's not his brother. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've realised it just now too, Your Honour. It seems not to be his brother, yes, but bearing in mind --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So I'm not the only one confused here. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Gerxhaliu, I'm going to show you yet another document; 3D64. It is a record from the military court attached to the command of the Pristina Corps, the number is KR 199/99. Actually, this record speaks of the same event like the last document, 3D63, except that it was drafted by the military organs that were there on site. Doctor, what about Seladin Gerxhaliu and Hatboma Gerxhaliu? Who are these people? They are relations of yours too, right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seladin Gerxhaliu is a cousin, yes. He's the son of my uncle. But the other person, Hatboma Gerxhaliu, I don't know who she is. I can read Cyrillics and as far as I can see, here it is Hatboma; it's spelled not accurately.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Is there a person in your family to whom this could pertain?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could pertain to Fatbardha. Fatbardha.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gerxhaliu, do you see that in the last paragraph of this statement - could it please be lowered a bit for the witness's benefit - it says here that the investigating judge together with his team went to the spot where the casing had allegedly been found and that that is only 300 metres away from your home, and that that is when the investigating judge's vehicle was hit as he was leaving the site.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: On what date?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: The date is the 5th of June 1999.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would appreciate if you do not confuse me with the dates, because this is when I went to Ulqin and I already mentioned that I heard that there were fighting but not in the vicinity of my house. There were no fightings in the vicinity of my house. Because the Serb forces, the army forces, and the police forces were there, nearby.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic, what do you say this document relates to? The investigation of what?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's an investigation of the murder of 12 persons that was carried out on the 5th of June 1999. This is the second stage of the investigation. As far as I managed to understand things --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Okay. I understood -- that's what I thought I understood until I see a reference to where the casing had allegedly been found. It wasn't an investigation into some --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour. The place where this casing was found, well the casing referred to, it's the relative called Hatboma or something along those lines. That is the cartridge or casing that she handed over to the police and she then directed them to the place where they found it. And when they tried to go there - it's only 300 metres away from his house - they were attacked in the way that was described in greater detail in the previous document, 3D63. They were attacked and they had to leave the vehicle behind, and one person was wounded, and so on and so forth, as described in the other document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please, it's not for you to give evidence. Please just confine your answers to the particular questions I ask you. And let's move on, because this witness has no direct knowledge of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: In your statement, doctor, on page -- just a moment, please. Paragraph 10, you stated that the convoy -- well, actually I'm taking you back now to the 2nd of May. The convoy that was moving from Slakovce to Vucitrn, that in that convoy there were about 40.000 persons. In your statement that you gave on the 18th of June 1999, and that's the statement that you gave in Ulcinj to the investigator of the Prosecutor's Office, you said that there were 20.000 persons in the convoy. How come there is this discrepancy, doctor, that the number of persons in the convoy was increased from 20.000 to 40.000?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I have to say that I don't read paragraph 10 as saying that. Perhaps paragraph 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 11. It's my mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Marcussen?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Maybe Mr. Visnjic could clarify what statement he's referring to when he refers to a statement of 18 June 1999. I'm aware of the existence of notes from an interview but not one which was carried out by the Office of the Prosecutor, so we may need to clarify what it is we are talking about. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you clarify that, please, Mr. Visnjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was my understanding that this was a document that is actually notes from an interview with representatives of the OTP. The number of the witness was 33 at the time, and the page is K00186 of his statement taken in Ulcinj on the 18th of June, 1999, and the person making the note was called Muriel Rodrigues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does that help, Mr. Marcussen?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I do have that. My case manager is checking one more time whether I'm correct on this but, as far as I know, this is not a statement or notes taken by OTP but by the International Crisis Group, but let's just clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I wouldn't put it that way because we got it on a completely different form. The form is completely different from that used by the ICG. Now, I don't know whether we yet again have a problem with your system.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The information I have about this document is these are notes taken by a person working for the ICG and that this is one of the examples of a document that was then put into a database.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, at the end of the day it doesn't matter who took it. The point is being made that it's a statement which is claimed to be different, although it may be it's not quite as simple as that. So let's have your question, Mr. Visnjic, and please bear in mind that we are interested in significant issues and not peripherally important matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the question was put to the doctor. On the 18th of June 1999, in your statement you say that there were 20.000 persons in the convoy, but then in 2000 you say that the number of persons in the convoy was 40.000. Could you please explain the discrepancy. And in the meantime, could we please see P1231, or rather, could it be prepared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Doctor, can you deal with the suggested discrepancy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I think it was in June that I gave my statement to the respected interviewer, and even then I said 40.000. It might be a mistake in translation or in writing. So I would like to emphasise once again that even then in Ulqin I said there were 40.000, and this was an approximate figure because I didn't actually count the number of persons. This is the number that I have stated then and later in the other statement, 40.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Doctor, when you said you were ordered by the KLA to leave the territory of Cecelija and Slakovce, since they could no longer defend it, what instruction was given to the civilians where to go? Were they told to follow the road to Vucitrn?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have stated in my statement as well that personally I was offered to go there but I joined my family in the column, and since there was no food and no hygiene equipment and there were some diseases that were being spread among the column, we were then forced to leave from Sllakovc in the direction Ceceli hoping that we would be able to get to Macedonia or Albania or Montenegro. Sorry, I just want to finish my thought. Please don't rush me. And this is for the benefit of the interpreters as well. So some of us were hoping that we will survive despite the fact that we were aware that we had to go through two positions in Rashica neighbourhood and in Sfaracak i Eperm and there I mentioned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Doctor, I have to interrupt you because you're not dealing with the question. And I'm afraid we have so much on paper here we have to confine ourselves to the particular questions that are being asked. Now, Mr. Visnjic, where is it we find this statement that he was ordered by the KLA to leave?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in the transcript of -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The question you were asked is, when you said earlier on Monday that you were ordered by the KLA to leave because they could no longer defend the territory, were you told to follow a particular road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. They didn't give us a direction that we were supposed to follow. They just said that they could no longer protect us, and that's why we were forced to take that road to go to Ceceli --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translations continues] ... that's the answer to the question. If Mr. Visnjic wants to ask another one, then he will do so. Let's try and confine the answers to the question that's asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Did they tell you to go to Macedonia or Albania, doctor?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Nobody did. But this was what we wanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I wanted to show you an OTP exhibit, P1231. It is a report of the MUP. Could you please direct your attention to paragraph 3, which states --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We don't have the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
