utterances.text: "The territory of the Vucitrn municipality was voluntarily abandoned by up to 17.000 -- between 17.000 and 19.000 inhabitants in their vehicles." In your knowledge, doctor, is this figure correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm it, because there was no way I could count them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm whether 8.000 people remained? Can you confirm that 8.000 people remained behind?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know, and I have said it in my statement, that my family -- from the 2nd to the 4th of May, my family was in the agriculture cooperative of Vushtrri, and because they had no means of going either to Albania or Macedonia, they returned. But as to how many went and as to how many were left behind, this is something I cannot confirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Therefore, your family wanted to go to Macedonia or Albania but they couldn't. They had no means by which to do that? This is your conclusion? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is my conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Visnjic. Mr. Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I believe my learned friend, Mr. Visnjic was very thorough and I will have just a questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Dr. Gerxhaliu. My name is Aleksandar Aleksic, and together with Mr. John Ackerman I appear on behalf of General Nebojsa Pavkovic. I will have a few questions for you. I will try to be as specific as possible, and I would kindly ask you to provide as concisely as possible, if possible with a yes or no. Dr. Gerxhaliu, the first statement that we have that was provided by you to anyone in relation to the events you've testified about is the statement given to an organisation called International Crisis Group. Do you remember having given such a statement to that organisation?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. What do you mean a statement? When, where?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Dr. Gerxhaliu, we received from the Prosecution your statement given to the International Crisis Group when you were in Ulcinj probably. We don't have such data as regards the actual date. It was probably on the 18th of June, 1999, when you were in Ulcinj still.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: And in that statement, you described several incidents. Incident number 3 is the event of the 2nd of May, and you said there that the convoy was approached by some forces, and in that statement given to the ICG you described those forces as paramilitaries who wore black and green masks and bandanas and their faces were painted; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Further on in the same statement given to the ICG, you mentioned the incident of the 31st of May, 1999, and you described those forces and when you spoke about the Serbian forces, you defined them as paramilitary forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were militaries and paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gerxhaliu, in your statement it says the witness has in mind paramilitary forces. Is this the way you put it, as regards the 31st of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It simply confirms that it doesn't appear to be a statement that's been recorded. It's been the impressions of whoever was speaking to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Also, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just hold on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As regards this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Dr. Gerxhaliu, you said you were a member of the KLA and that during the day you worked at the state hospital and at night you went to field hospitals of the KLA to treat members of the KLA as of 1998; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever treat a wounded Serb, having in mind Hippocrates oath?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have an opportunity to treat any injured Serb because they -- if there were any, they didn't bring them to our hospital but to a more equipped ward in the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Further on in your statement given to the OTP, on page 3, and I don't believe this is in dispute, that there was every day fighting between KLA -- the KLA and the Serb army, and so you were busy all the time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was very busy all the time, that is correct. Because I was almost the only one that is doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us how close you were to the fighting, what was the closest distance that you were from the fighting?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never been in the fighting, where the fighting took place. I was always in the hospital which today has been turned into a museum. I heard the shots, but the distance was several kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Further on in your statement you describe that on the 31st of May in the morning around 4.00 a.m. you found out that two hand-grenades were thrown at the old Serbian barracks. Is this what you said?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not hand-grenades, but they were two explosions from the NATO forces thrown against that barracks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Which paragraph is that, Mr. Aleksic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is on page 7, paragraph 2, the 28th paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Dr. Gerxhaliu, I didn't have hand-grenades in mind but actual bombs dropped from planes, but you've clarified that. Yesterday in the transcript page 8, lines 15 and 16, you said that there was quite a lot of ammunition at the barracks. Do you know whether there was anyone at the barracks, or in the barracks?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I only know that it was an old barracks and that it was bombed by the NATO planes. It says here "two bombs." I don't know what exactly they were, but I do know that there were two huge explosions which woke us up in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The last question: At the end of your statement, you say that you left Kosovo, and after having crossed over to Serbia there were no further problems; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Aleksic. Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I've got some questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Dr. Gerxhaliu. My name is Djuro Cepic, one of the counsel for General Vladimir Lazarevic. I will have a few questions for you, and to try to be as expeditious as possible, please provide concise answers. And I will try to be as clear as possible in my questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we please have P4 put on the screen, at 4 minutes 20 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Stop here.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask for the footage to be stopped here. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: The person we see on the screen, you will agree with me that he's wearing a former JNA uniform or, rather, the uniform of the army of Yugoslavia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see that very clearly. I see his back.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I was interested in the coat and the colour of it.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very unclear. It's unclear for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Is it clear to you who it is in that picture?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I don't know who the person is, but I see some Albanians here.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that this was a member of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot agree or disagree. I don't see any emblem, any insignia, and the picture is not clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Dr. Gerxhaliu, what sort of uniforms did the KLA wear?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had camouflage, green camouflage uniforms, and they had their own emblems on which it was written, KLA. The military police wore dark uniforms, black uniforms, with the emblems as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did members of the KLA wore [as interpreted] civilian clothes alongside their weapons?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we continue with the footage, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, before you move on, what does -- is this supposed to be, this film?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is an exhibit brought here by this witness showing the column on the 2nd of May. The witness stated that the members of the KLA wore such and such uniforms of such and such colours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I just want to identify what this film is. It's not referred to in the witness statement, I don't think, is it? I just want to be clear what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This footage was part of the set of OTP exhibits proposed to be used by -- with this witness. It concerns the event on the 2nd of May. That's at least how I understood it. And we received this among other exhibits from the Prosecution. It is P4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I do agree with my learned colleague that it concerns the event on the 2nd of May. It's my understanding that it's a video taken after the event, so the 3rd or the 4th or something like that, so it's not showing the actual column, what might have been in connection with the burials or something like that. It was brought in by another witness than this one, as far as I can see from this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's sufficient for present purposes, thank you. Carry on, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we continue with the footage?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So as not to waste time, could we rewind a minute, by a minute? Back, back. As of 3 minutes 20 seconds, can we stop here? At 3.30, 3 minutes 30 seconds. 3 minutes, 30 seconds. A bit further. Stop now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Is this a KLA member that we see here?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: To his right is there another member of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can't see it very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can we continue with the footage, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: To the right of the person in this uniform, is this another member of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recognise him. I recognise the first because of his uniform and his emblem. But for the second, maybe he's a member of the military police of the KLA or someone who has taken the weapon from someone else. I can't confirm the person wearing the uniform, that he is a member.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Well, if he was a military policeman of the KLA he seems to be wearing civilian clothes. My question is: Did this member of the KLA military police wear civilian clothes, the person carrying a rifle in his right arm? With the wooden butt?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person wearing civilian clothes, I'm not sure whether he's wearing civilian clothes or whether he's dressed in black uniform. Maybe he has taken the weapon from this other member of the KLA. Maybe he's carrying the weapon from him. I was a civilian myself and never carried any weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen you had a comment to make.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I think it became clear on the record. I don't think the witness said that this was a KLA military police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: He didn't say that the first time either so -- yes. The position is clear that he claims not to know. Yes, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Why does he have a backpack and a rifle in his right arm? The same with the one in uniform? They both have backpacks.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that he's carrying the weapon of the person wearing a uniform. At least this is my assumption. I cannot confirm it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we continue with the footage, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop here, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: This person wearing a dark jacket, a ski-jacket, he is holding something on his back. Would you agree that this is yet another KLA member?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I do not agree with that. The members of the KLA, all of them wore uniforms, carried weapons and were different from the civilians. I was the only one in the KLA in being a civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Why did the person we named wear camouflage pants and a ski-jacket and he has something on his back? And we may discuss later what that is.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think these are details which we should not discuss here. I said it quite clearly that whoever was a member had to carry -- to wear a uniform and carry weapons. Maybe in this case we see someone who is leaving his weapon with a friend or with an acquaintance for going somewhere or eating something or greeting somebody. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we continue with the footage?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Only if you're moving to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Your Honour. I do apologise, but I have got some more questions about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You have no reason to apologise. If I think you've exhausted the subject, I'll let you know. But it's for you to conduct your own cross-examination, subject to control if we think it's not productive.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. [Interpretation] Could we please see the film now? We don't need to have it rewound.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What is this on the shoulder of this person wearing a vest, the person we discussed a few moments ago? The vest is civilian.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you move it a little bit so that I can see it better?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see him carrying anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, it looks as though he has something on his shoulder, does it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you rewind it, please? Because you asked me about what he's carrying on his back. I don't see what he's carrying on his back.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He's not carrying anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's this person with the purplish coloured jacket, padded jacket, whose left hand you can now see in the photograph adjacent to the cap of the man in front. What is that he has over his shoulder?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean this person on the opposite side?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The one in the middle.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in the middle, the one who is wearing this dark purplish colour jacket?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think he has something which resembles a weapon, but the other one, nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please continue with the film from 4.00?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you just play the film, please? Stop here, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: The right-hand side, black jacket, jeans, a cap with some insignia, and in the right-hand an automatic rifle. Is that a member of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And what do you think, then, who is this strolling about freely with a weapon like that? Is it perhaps a Serb soldier?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He may be a relative of the soldier who has left his weapon with him to do some other thing. I can't see very well his cap. Maybe the cap, too, belongs to that -- the other soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And the one on the very left, who figures so prominently, is that perhaps somebody's relative, too, with a rifle in his hand? Yes, that's the one, also in civilian clothing.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I wasn't present there but this is what I think. As far as I know, all the KLA members were armed, but it may happen at a moment that you may leave your weapon with someone else to go and take care of some of your business.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Now you're claiming that you were not in the refugee convoy, and before that you said that you were. What is true out of these two?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The truth is that I was somewhere in the middle of the convoy, not here where you allege, because as I said this column was kilometres long.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No doubt you're going to make a point about the date, are you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Trust us to be able to work these things out, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a second. Doctor, it may be suggested that people with loyalty to their fellow Albanians, who were involved in this conflict, might feel that it's a point of honour to maintain that civilians or at least people who during the day were civilians and at other times took up arms did not in fact do so, that the KLA was an entirely military, organised organisation because it's felt that the civilians who helped and went as far as to bear arms and use them ought to be protected. Now, if you were to be thinking that, that you ought to protect people here in giving evidence, then you would be very misguided because you would be doing no service to the people in Kosovo who expect justice here. It's vital that we are told the whole truth. The oath, the declaration is to tell the whole truth. Now, that is not a comment on your evidence. It is an expression of concern that we do hear things said about people in civilian clothes engaging in fighting or fighting -- activities associated with fighting against Serb forces. And we are anxious to get to the truth of that, and we know that you were a doctor treating fighters who were wounded. So please bear these things in mind when you're answering questions from counsel about whether people who were involved with the KLA were, in fact, on occasions simply dressed at least partially in civilian clothing rather than a regular uniform. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Dr. Gerxhaliu, did you do your military service in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, I would like to add just a sentence, Your Honour, an explanation. I have made the solemn declaration to tell the truth, and as I said, I can neither confirm or deny whether there were KLA in civilian clothes. I only can confirm things that I have seen with my own eyes. If I have seen only uniformed KLA members, this is what I can claim and confirm. It is my wish as well for those responsible to be held responsible, because the innocent, regardless of their ethnic background, should live together and approach the democratic world and Europe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Doctor, I understand that, and I also acknowledge readily that you have made many statements which anyone listening to this case would regard as concessions about the activities of the KLA. You've clearly been frank about many aspects of the activity of the KLA. But you'll understand our concern when every time you're shown a picture of a man with a weapon you think he might just be keeping it for a friend. It's very difficult applying simple common sense to accept that, that explanation. So that's why I say to you to exercise great caution when you're answering these questions. Now, let's hear what the next question is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would then like to move on to another area. We have received clear answers here; at least that is my view.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In your statement you described where the convoy moved, from Slakovce to Cecelija and then further on in the direction of Gornja and Donja Sudimlja, so from north to south. Is that not the exact direction?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Further on, on page 4 paragraph 5 the English translation, and page 5, paragraph 5 of the Albanian translation you say that near the convoy there were members of the Serb army and paramilitaries and that they came from the north while you were hiding on your tractor trailer in order not to be recognised. Were you afraid that some of the local Serbs would recognise you?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was afraid of everybody, because regardless of everything, the local Serbs armed, the military, the paramilitary, they were executing all the young people from the column, and I have testified about certain incidents that occurred in that part of the column that I was part of.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: That's not what I asked you. Doctor, sir, could you please give clear and concise answers to my questions? My next question is: The persons who approached the convoy, did they have bandanas around their necks?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were with bandanas and without bandanas, and they were also in different uniform, because as I said, they approached our column on four occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: With paint on their faces, right? Paint on their faces, right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Aged between 30 and 40, right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Listen, it was becoming dark and I could not really tell their age, but they were of different ages, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And these aren't persons that we saw a few moments ago from the column. Where were they at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were on the 3rd of June. We are speaking now of 2nd of June, of that night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We are talking about May, May and not June. But the question is perfectly valid. The question is: Even though the film may have been taken on the 3rd or 4th of May, where were the people we see in that photograph on the 2nd of May? Have I understood the question correctly?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely, Your Honour. But at this point in time, we are talking about the night of the 2nd of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The question is: Where were the people we saw in the pictures on the 2nd of May? Did you see any of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The KLA members, as I said in my statement, they took the wounded on the 2nd of May, and together with the KLA unit they set off in the direction of Dumnica in a more strategic place. So the KLA part had been -- had abandoned the column. It was only me from the KLA as a civilian there. While on the 3rd, when this film was made, they came back, they took these positions, in order for the burial of the victims to be able to be carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How far did the convoy get on the 2nd of June -- or rather, I'm sorry, the 3rd of May? Where did the convoy stop on the 3rd of May?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no column on the 3rd of May. Only those from the convoy who survived, they settled in the agricultural cooperative, while I went back to the place, to the original place from where I set off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, what were we looking at in the film, then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was probably filmed on the day when the KLA soldiers repositioned themselves there in order to bury the dead. And those vehicles, those tractors that had remained there, as I said, on the 3rd of May the road was full of tractors and vehicles. Some of them were burned, some of them were not burned, some of them were damaged. And near these tractors and vehicles, as I've mentioned it in my statement, there were more than 100 people who had been killed. There were more than 100 bodies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But are you saying that the film does not show a column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that this was filmed on the 3rd of May. And the footage does not show the column because, as I said, there was no column after the 3rd of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, by your leave, if you permit me, well, I hope I won't take up too much of the Court's time, if you allow me to show a bit more of the film where we can see where the column is moving. Could you just give us a moment, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Is this not a column that is moving, Dr. Gerxhaliu, sir?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But this is from the 3rd of May, those who remained. Because not all the 40.000 of them could go to the cooperative on the 2nd of May. This is how it should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your claim was that on the 2nd of May in the evening, the column was completely broken and practically no longer existed, right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 2nd of May, the column split into two. One part went to the cooperative and the other, you know what happened, some of them were killed, about 200 people. So on the 3rd of May, many people came back there to see what had happened and then they all gathered together in order to do the burial service.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: If you said that in the column there were 40.000 persons and that 200 got killed, then there is a remaining 39.800. What about these 39.800 people? Where were they? How many of them went to Zadruga, the cooperative?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't possibly know that, how many of them went to the cooperative. It was dark, and it was a matter of to be or not to be, as the English say. I know that the majority went there, but there was another part that remained and they came the next morning to see who had survived, who had left, and to attend the burial ceremony.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Doctor, if on every tractor trailer there was an average of, say, five people, how long should the column be for it to include 40.000 people?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were more than five in tractors. There were other vehicles as well, not only tractors, and many, many on foot. And the majority actually were walking on foot. There were people in carts, in cars, and so on. So to my opinion, the column was several kilometres long. Unfortunately, I wasn't able to measure it from one Studime to the other, but I know it was long. And to my estimate, there were about 40.000 in the column, and even more.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Dr. Gerxhaliu, could you please give me the kilometres involved? The distance from Slakovce to Cecelija, how far away is that? And then also what the distance is to Gornja Sudimlja.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have actually never measured the distance, but I know that Sllakovc and Ceceli are close to each other and that you can travel this distance in half an hour. And from Ceceli to Studime e Eperme, you have to climb a hill and then again go downhill, so it is a difficult road to do on foot, but at that time I was thinner, about ten kilograms, I had ten kilograms less so I could move better. As I said in the beginning, I never mentioned [as interpreted] the distance, and you can ask experts about the distance, not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So you don't have an exact idea about distances in the area where you were born?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: That issue was of no interest to me, because I rarely went on that side during the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I suspect the end of the last answer was "I never measured distance" rather than "mentioned." I may be wrong, but perhaps the interpreters can listen again to that and check it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters confirm that it was measured, not mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you believe this would be a good moment, perhaps we could take the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Have you much more to ask?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Up to ten minutes, up to 15, depends of answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And are we likely to finish with this witness today or not? Do you know? Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'll try, Your Honour. I'm going to use the break to cull through my questions to remove some. It's my desire to finish and have time for the Prosecution to redirect the witness as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's helpful, thank you. So we'll resume at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: To go back to where we left off before the break, Dr. Gerxhaliu, the way you described the column with the number of people and the way it moved, in my rough estimate, that column would have to have been 40 kilometres long which would be exactly the distance between Kosovska Mitrovica and Pristina. The distance between Slakovce, if one goes across Gornja Sudimlja to Donja Sudimlja, is about three and a half kilometres. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's not possible that it is only three and a half kilometres, because from my house to Studime e Eperme one should travel about an hour on foot. This can't even be as crow flies, let alone the realistic distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Not more than 15 kilometres tops?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be, more or less. And since I have not measured it myself, the distance that you just gave me cannot be absolute.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. To move on to something else then. Today, in the transcript, you mentioned this. This concerns the event on the 2nd of May, 1999, when I asked you about the people who approached the convoy, and that was page 59 of today's transcript, you said that it was getting dark and that you couldn't clearly make out what they looked like and how old they were. You said some of them had bandanas around their necks and that they wore different uniforms. I presume you didn't see the caps they were wearing. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was difficult for me to observe everything because I was half hidden in the tractor, as I said in my statement. I mainly heard what they said, their offensives, the communications between them. I could not observe very much. I could to some extent but mainly I heard things spoken by them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I thank you. In that same statement, you mentioned that those very people whom you couldn't clearly see arrived in personnel -- armoured personnel carriers and in some jeeps; is that correct? Is that correct in your statement?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They came in vehicles, APCs, transporters, Pinzgauers, with every single military equipment they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Of course, since you were hidden and as you've described earlier, you couldn't see that in any great detail; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't hidden. I was half hidden. I could see some things and I couldn't see other things. And as I said I could mainly hear things, what they were speaking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that it wasn't only the military who had APCs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how the army, Yugoslav army, was organised at that time. Maybe the police had these kinds of vehicles as well. I have only stated things that I've seen myself in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You will agree with me that you could remember these events best back in 1999, immediately after they had taken place, isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: These events are engraved in my mind, and I will never forget them. I mentioned earlier that I have a diary, where I have noted down these events. These events are very difficult to speak of today, maybe less for me because I'm a doctor, but for others it is surely difficult to recall these events.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Dr. Gerxhaliu, on the 18th of June, 1999, you gave a statement in Ulcinj. That statement is a proposed exhibit by the OTP in these proceedings. In that statement, you described some material facts differently. You stated that the people who approached the convoy looked more like paramilitaries than the police, that they were masked, that they had painted faces, and that they wore green or black bandanas. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Cepic, are you now quoting what someone has noted as his impression of what the witness said rather than the word for word account of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I quote from the material received from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you can see it and I can't see it. Has it got a number that can come up on the screen for us? No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: May I have a minute, please? May I have a minute, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the English, it is page K0218781.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No. The only relevant number will be one of the e-court numbers. Now, it doesn't sound as though you have put this into e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour, but this was in the set of proposed exhibits by the OTP. It was forwarded to us by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It can only be a proposed exhibit if it has a P number and it was in the 65 ter summary produced by the Prosecution. This is taking up too much time. I'm not going to allow you to question on this since we don't have the exhibit to see and we have got reason from previous questions to think that it's an account recorded by the witness -- by the interviewer of his or her impression of what was said rather than a word-for-word account of the witness. So let's move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. It wasn't my intention to waste any precious time. I just wanted to indicate what we have received from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gerxhaliu, in your statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, hold on. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'm just slightly concerned about the evidence, the way it looks on the record now. I think we've sorted out this is not a Prosecution exhibit, it's not a proposed Prosecution exhibit. I have the document with me here, and maybe my colleague would stipulate to the fact that on the first page of document it actually says that, "In the field we were surrounded by Serb forces, police and military." There is not only mention of paramilitaries. Just because the record seems to be a little unclear on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we work on evidence, we don't work on questions, Mr. Marcussen. That's quite unnecessary. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Dr. Gerxhaliu, in your statement from 2000, you stated, and you confirmed this yesterday as it is part of the transcript, you described the bombing. This is in your statement, in the English, page 3, paragraph 3; in the Albanian, page 4, paragraph 1; and in the B/C/S, page 3, paragraph 3. You state there, as you moved alongside the brook, that you were under fire from the tanks and that the leaves and branches were being torn off the trees. Of course, you couldn't see those tanks; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already mentioned earlier that the stream was about 2 to 3 metres deep, and the tanks were firing from the hill at Rashica neighbourhood. And when they were firing, the bullets would cut the branches. And whenever this occurred, we would stop our journey and we could not move, of course, because otherwise we would have been hit. And it is true that I could not see exactly where they were. When they were shooting, as I said, we would take shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: If I understand this correctly, you were at a lower altitude, you were quite lower than the tanks themselves; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. The tanks were positioned on two strategic hills from where they could control Sfaracak, Studime e Poshteme, and up to Vushtrri, that entire territory. The stream was down --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: That suffices. Thank you, Doctor. I suppose you have no particular knowledge of ballistics; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm a doctor and I have no knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know, Doctor, that a tank cannot open fire at a negative angle or, to put it plainly, it cannot target anything that is at a lower altitude than the tank itself?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Listen, there were not only tanks there. There were rocket launchers; there were all sorts of military equipment. And these branches, these trees that were hit, they were quite higher. And that's why we were not that scared that the bullets would hit us, because we were lower, near the stream.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Now you say "bullets". Previously you had said tank shells. Which of the two is correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only say that they were firing from all sorts of military equipment. As I said, the trees above our heads were hit. And now whether they were hit by shrapnels or bullets or other projectiles, I don't know. I just know that the branches fell on the ground, and when the firing occurred we would take shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the Milosevic case transcript, you claimed that those VJ positions were targeted very precisely by NATO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we speak of the barracks situated at the exit of Vushtrri, on the right-hand side --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I wasn't asking you about the barracks. It was something else and I can quote it to you. This is from the Milosevic case, transcript page 4123, the 2nd of May, 2002. The question was being posed about the NATO bombing, and the answer was, "In our area NATO bombs were very precise and they only targeted Serbian military positions." Is what you stated then correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. NATO targeted very precisely, and I actually verified this after the war, where the shells had fallen.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In your statement, in paragraph 28, and Mr. Aleksic had a question about that as well, you state that on the 31st of May, around 4.00 a.m., the Vucitrn barracks was bombed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said it was correct even earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What would you say if I said or if I put it to you that that night, it wasn't the barracks that was hit but, rather, the factory in Vucitrn called Mile Zakic?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no factory by that name in Vushtrri, only the Llamkos factory there exists, and I've actually brought the list with the names of persons who abandoned their work in this factory and joined the army. This is the first time I hear about this factory Mile Zakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I wasn't asking you about that, Mr. Gerxhaliu. Thank you, doctor.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it necessary for me to explain this, Your Honours? I want to state again that there is no factory by that name in Vushtrri.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. We've got that answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I haven't got any further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cepic. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. My name is Dan Ivetic, and I'm one of the attorneys representing Mr. Sreten Lukic along with my colleagues Mr. Branko Lukic and Mr. Ozren Ogrizovic today, and I've got a set of questions for you that I hope we can go through in the time we have left here today.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: My first question relates to an area that I believe was left open but one of my colleagues, Mr. Visnjic, I believe it was tendered to everyone Exhibit 3D71, and I would ask if you still have that in exhibit in front of you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We require to have it on the screen there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe this was the exhibit that was only in hard form that Mr. Visnjic had distributed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I see you have it in front of you, sir. I'll wait for the Bench to have a copy as well. Now, sir, this booklet, this Kosovo Liberation Army martyrs, if could direct your attention to -- it's the 4th page from the front in the copy that I have, hopefully it's the same as yours. I apologise. This is not an exhibit that I had prepared. But there is a photograph of an individual, one of these Kosovo Liberation Army martyrs with the name Seladin Gerxhaliu. And I would like to ask you, sir, is this a photograph of the man that was your cousin and your neighbour that you testified earlier today regarding his burial on the 31st of May, 1999? Is that this person?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I greet you as well, Mr. Ivetic. Yes, this is that person I testified about, Seladin.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would, I guess, move to tender this exhibit into evidence since I believe my colleague failed to do so. Now, doctor --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Doctor, you testified regarding your work treating KLA wounded, and you gave us the approximate positions of KLA field hospitals in the Vucitrn municipality. I want to ask you if you could briefly tell us where were the main KLA bases located in the area?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know all the bases, where the KLA bases were, but I heard that there was one in Melenica, in Majden, in the areas near Studime e Eperme, in Dumnica, and in some other locations. My aim was to be there as a doctor, to work with wounded and with ill people.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Well let me ask you this question, then: Isn't it true that on the 27th of March, 1999, you and your family decided to go to Slakovce because there was a large KLA presence there, some sort of base or post? Is that accurate or not?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in Sllakovc, but from Studime e Eperme and above, it was an area protected by the KLA. I don't know exactly the strength of KLA in that area, but my wife has some relatives there and that's where I actually would stay and at the same time carry out my professional duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Now, if I can direct your attention to your written statement that has been tendered by the Office of the Prosecutor, that's Exhibit P2275. At paragraph 7 of that written statement, you describe how persons that you state were the police came to your home looking for you. I want to ask you: Was it widely known within the community that you worked with and were a member of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was public knowledge. Everybody knew. It was a voluntary army. Nobody forced me to become a member, and of course my duties towards the nation and the wish to liberate ourselves made me become one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, you earlier in your testimony today said that we have to make a clear distinction between what you actually saw and heard and what you heard from others. And I want to ask you, yesterday or -- excuse me, Monday you testified that your family left due to some orders that had been issued, and I want to make very clear you yourself personally did not witness any orders being given for your family to vacate their home. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day, when my family left, I was at the clinic and I received this order there. As I mentioned in my statement, it was issued to me by the then director of the clinic. As for the Rashica Svarcali families, they all had received the order, and by the time I got there, they had already left. Just for explanation, the Rashica family, they set off for Pristina but they were returned at the Dakovce check-point. When they came back in April --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think you've already testified to that earlier. I just want a clarification of that point and then we can move on because we are short on time, and I'm trying to complete your testimony today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I ask you one question at this stage? You've confirmed membership of the KLA to Mr. Ivetic. Did you wear a uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I never had a KLA uniform but I was a member of the KLA, and I was a fan of the KLA but I never had a uniform.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, isn't it a fact that your family left their home in or about April of 1999 due to the fact that persons whom you said were the police came and asked for you and said they would keep coming back to ask for you until they found you? Isn't that the real reason that you left, that your family left, and that it wasn't due to any orders that were issued by anyone?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a lot of movement. My family, when they fled the first time in March, it was pursuant to this order that was issued in every single neighbourhood. And I moved quite a lot. I came back to the house on several occasions, once in April and then in May, then again in late May. And in April when they came, they collected some vehicles. They asked my wife where I was, and I was hiding in the house of a neighbour, her name was Shana [phoen]. When I would go back home I usually wouldn't stay very long, I would just check how they were doing. It even happened --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- that I didn't see my family for two or three weeks in a row.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay, sir, if I could interrupt you now. This incident that you're talking about in April, first of all, did you in fact see with your own eyes the individuals who came to your house to ask about you? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I had already left.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So would it be safe to say, then, that the description of this person is based upon your wife and not what you had actually seen?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which person do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The persons that came to your house sometime between 7 and 10 April. That is referenced in paragraph 7 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: My wife talked to them, as I explained in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And with respect to -- okay. With respect to the map that you drew on the other day, the area that you had outlined there only consisted of the portions of the municipality where the KLA had 100 per cent control of villages; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please? Because I wasn't focused.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, sir. On Monday the Prosecutor had you draw several lines on a map showing areas that were under the control of the KLA. Now I wanted to ask you a question to clear that up. The lines that you drew, that reflected areas that were completely under the control of the KLA but did not reflect areas where the KLA had sympathisers or personnel located, is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is accurate. From the lines I drew in the direction of the mountain, that was the area controlled by the KLA, whereas from the 8th of January, when eight soldiers were captured they made preparations and launched an attack and massacred us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We are not going to get through this unless I ask more focused questions, sir. With respect to the presence of the KLA, is it a fact that the KLA did have personnel and sympathisers in areas that were held by Serbs including within the city of Vucitrn itself, or Vushtrri as it's in the Albanian?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. There must have been. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Are you familiar with some of the surrounding villages such as Bukosh village?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of any KLA presence in Bukosh village at any time in 1998 or 1999?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because Bukosh is on the other side of the river. It's very far away from us. I've never been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, as far as your services with the KLA were concerned, is it a fair statement to state that your services were needed in greater frequency after October of 1998, that is to say after the Milosevic-Holbrooke accords because the KLA tried to step up its activities and attacks at that time?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know were they needed in much or less, but I do know that whenever they needed me I went because as I have taken the Hippocrates oath, my duty was to give assistance to each and every one. So I can only tell you that I've never made any distinctions to the people I provided assistance to.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you ever have to take an oath to the KLA, sir? And if so, what was that oath?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never took any oath, only the Hippocrates oath when I graduated from my faculty.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And as far as the armaments that you saw with the UCKA/KLA, was it accurate to state that they were armed with automatic, that is to say Kalashnikov rifles?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not well-versed in armaments but usually they had Kalashnikovs, small bombs, maybe others, but where I worked I didn't see much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you also notice them to have mortars or zolja rocket launchers?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never saw them. I only looked after my job.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you have knowledge of the fact that when the KLA took over a village, persons that did not support the KLA, be they Serb civilians or Albanian or other minority civilians, did you have knowledge that these persons who did not support the KLA were then expelled from that village by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never had any such knowledge. That's the first time to hear it. When I was asked that in September 1998, all Albanians were victim, and I don't know what Mr. Visnjic asked me about, he didn't explain to me the names of the persons involved, so this is the first time for me to hear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If I can perhaps use your own words to better describe it. Would it be safe to say you can neither confirm nor deny that fact, of the KLA expelling persons from their villages?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw it. How can I lie? I have sworn to tell the truth and I can only testify to what I have seen and heard. I never heard or saw anyone being expelled from the village or from their homes by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Perhaps there was a translation error. I did not mean to imply that you were lying or anything else. I was just trying to clarify. Now, if I can direct you to something that you did say that you had knowledge of, at around paragraph 11 of your written statement to the Office of the Prosecutor, you describe how, on the 2nd of May, 1999, an order came from the KLA for the Albanian civilians to leave the area. Now I want to ask you, sir, as a member of the KLA or UCK, was it the standard operating procedures of the KLA to order populations living under their control to leave specified areas?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was any strict order per se. It was kind of a warning to the people telling them that the positions in Llap and Shala had fallen in the hands of the enemy so they should leave, lest they should fall into the hands of the Serb forces who were advancing in the direction of Sllakovc.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I just want to make it clear the beginning of that answer, as I heard it, was it was not any strict order per se.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's how I heard it as well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir what I'm asking you is to your knowledge, had such orders come from the KLA previously or subsequently to May the 2nd in other occurrences?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And by the way how were such orders communicated by the KLA to the general population?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the 2nd of May order?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a member of the KLA who had information on what was going on on the front line, and he told us to leave, not by any specific order. He told us that the positions of the KLA were taken by the Serb forces and that -- Yugoslav forces, and that this was a kind of order. At least this is how we saw it, kind of instruction, better say.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And after that, sir, you went to join your family in the convoy. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: My family was not very far from the hospital where I worked, so I went to greet my family. They took me with them. They wished me to join them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And no one from the KLA tried to stop you from joining your family. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no one. They asked me to join the wounded and the injured. And then they said, "We will wait for the last person to come, the injured person to come and we will not surrender so you make your own decision," they told me. My wife and my children asked me to go with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is it possible, sir, that other members of the KLA were given the similar decision to make and likewise went to join their families in the convoy?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other members of the KLA didn't have their families close by. At least I have no knowledge of that. I have said several times that as far as I could see, I was the only one there because I moved about the convoy when some co-villagers asked me to go here and there, at least from what I could see, from the mid-part of the convoy until where that man, Ibrahim Mulliqi, was with that white flag in his hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, sir, at paragraph 15 of your statement, you describe how certain armed persons approached the convoy around 5.00 p.m. and began approaching tractors and asking persons for money. Now, in the next paragraph you describe a variety of uniforms worn by these men, and I want to ask you some very specific questions relating to this description so that we can be clear. First of all, is it accurate to state that you did not see members of the Serbian police, that is to say of the Ministry of Interior, present at this time?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have said several times in this case I heard more than I could see, because dusk was falling and I am fully convinced that there was a cooperation of the forces of the Interior and of the army and the part of reservists, whatever they were, military forces or paramilitaries, they were there altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, prior to this occasion, prior to this incident, did you have occasion to view and become familiar with the uniforms worn by the police, worn by the members of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked in the city until before the NATO air-strikes. Of course, I have seen them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And could you please describe for us in detail the standard police uniform that you had knowledge of?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, that uniform was kind of blue camouflage uniforms, whereas the army wore green uniforms. The paramilitaries wore different uniforms with bandanas and stuff.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm asking you to focus right now on just the Ministry of Interior uniforms. Did those uniforms have anything on the sleeves or on the chest?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the sleeves, they had something, but that night, in the semi-darkness, I could see that there was -- that -- there were, as I said, blue camouflage and green camouflage uniforms, but I couldn't concentrate because, as I said, I was half in hiding.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So would it be fair to state, then, sir, that on that night, and I think we are talking about the night of May the 2nd, you could not verify whether in fact the uniforms that you saw, in particular the blue uniforms you saw, whether they had anything on their sleeves or on their chest? Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot ascertain [as interpreted] that I saw them explicitly because from the position I was hiding, it was impossible for me to do that, but I fully know and everybody said that, that there were forces from all these other bodies that I mentioned. They were all involved in that operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'm going to again direct to your own words earlier today, did you in fact not state in response to a question posed by one of my colleagues that you must make a clear distinction between what you saw and what you heard? And I would ask that your answers be very clear here as to what you personally saw, and I think you have -- your answer has stated that you were unable to see based upon where you were at, so I will move on. Now, at paragraph -- strike that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think before you go on that I certainly couldn't assume that at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think he said that he saw -- he said what he was able to see and then he said his conclusions were based on what other people, everyone knew, everyone saw. I mean, I could ask him some more questions on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If you're happy with that then you may move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, I guess maybe it's more important whether the Trial Chamber is happy with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah. The answer that was given, I'm also unsure about whether it's accurate at the beginning, where it says "I cannot ascertain that I saw them explicitly." I suspect that is that "I cannot assert that I saw them explicitly." Because he -- it was impossible for him to see. All right. I think you can move on to that -- from that. Well, just perhaps one question. Doctor, did you actually see what the personnel who came to the convoy were wearing with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw them wearing blue, black and green camouflage uniforms, and I heard those wearing blue and dark uniforms talking to my wife, asking her to give them money, which I gave to my daughter, and she gave the money to those people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, there you have it, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I guess my follow-up would be, which I may have already asked but I'll see. With respect to these individuals, sir, that you saw wearing these various coloured uniforms, am I correct that you could not see or discern, I should say, any of the shoulders or any markings on the uniforms?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was impossible for me to discern the markings in that semi-darkness and I not even thought of looking at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. That is very clear for me. Now if I can move on, at -- would it be safe to say, then, sir, that other persons -- well, strike that. Let's just go on to this one. Now, you later talk about the time-period around 11 -- between 11.00 and 12.00 at night, and you describe certain vehicles that came from the direction of Vucitrn, or Vushtrri, and state that there were two or three typical police cars in that. Now, first of all, I want to ask you is: It accurate that these vehicles came from the exact opposite direction that the other armed personnel you described previously came from?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they came from Vushtrri in the direction of upper, or eperme, Vushtrri. Studime, correction. I was listening to what they were saying. May -- am I allowed to quote what they said?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if it's responsive to my question. I think you've answered my question, and we are very close on time so I would prefer to move on to try to and complete you so as not to have you come back tomorrow. Now, could you describe for us these typical police vehicles, what they looked like? I know you've already testified that you could not discern the colour but could you describe these vehicles by appearance, by make?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This is which paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This is at paragraph 24 of the statement, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please answer that, doctor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I have explained it here. They came in vehicles Zastava 1. I couldn't discern the colour very well but I know that they were green -- sorry, blue colour. I think they were police and army vehicles, and they came -- approached to the place where I was taking shelter. And they said, among themselves, "We must purge the terrain." Clear the terrain. And at the moment they stopped, and one of them, probably he was the leader, he said, "Let's go back because we have no fuel left." And where I was hiding, I saw them turn back, going back to where they came, and corpses were lying on both sides of the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, if I could direct your attention to two paragraphs above from this paragraph, at paragraph 22. You described things that your wife later told you had happened. Am I correct that you did not witness any of the events that are described at paragraph 22 that your wife told you about?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: What things are you asking me about?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The persons that were dragged out of their vehicles and shot.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe you have mixed up the things. What persons were dragged out of the cars to be shot? Are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At paragraph 22 of your statement you describe certain things that you heard from your wife regarding persons dragged down and shot dead. And I want to ask you about those events. Now, I think it's clear that you heard those from your wife rather than witnessing them. Let me ask you this: Is it possible as far as you're wife is concerned that she has less familiarity with the recognition of uniforms than you do?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, my wife has got nothing to do with this column that was -- that came back because after my wife left with her part of the convoy, to the agricultural cooperatives, the others returned with their -- the people in the vehicles returned with their flash-lights on as I have said here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're being asked a specific question. You should have a number 22 against one of the paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's my understanding the Albanian is also numbered identically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If you look at number 22 you'll see the second sentence and it's talking about --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the family in the tractor in front of yours being dragged down and the question you're being asked is whether your wife would have less ability to recognise a uniform accurately than you would.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Both my wife and I can distinguish uniforms. That's not a problem. These people were in a tractor close to us. They were mostly our relatives. Because 36 people of Gerxhaliu family are dead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Doctor, please confine your answer to the question which is entirely related to the uniform recognition. Nothing to do with any of the events themselves. Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, you talk about when the vehicles left in the middle of the night, we are back to paragraph 24, when those vehicles left, how long after those vehicles left did it take for the KLA to appear to start collecting and burying bodies?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The KLA came on the next day, on the 3rd of June [as interpreted], but I didn't see them because I came later. I was very exhausted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour the transcript says 3rd of June. I believe I heard 3rd of May and I think we are clear on that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It should be the 3rd of May.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, it should be the 3rd of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir I think you actually said that and it just came out wrong in the transcript. Now is that the time when you treated a certain individual with a bullet in the forehead named Jetish Xhafa from Svracak village?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was taken with his father to be buried but then someone brought him to hospital. He had lost consciousness. He was injured. I saw that he was alive. I gave him the necessary aid, and I had to remove a bullet from his forehead.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, the bullet that you removed, was it whole or a fragment?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a bullet, a whole bullet. I think he still has the bullet to this day. I could manage to take out the bullet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you ascertain whether the bullet was from a pistol or a rifle?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think from a rifle, automatic rifle, but I can't be sure. As I said I have little knowledge of weapons, a knowledge I never wish to have.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, based upon your medical experience, first of all what area of medical specialty do you hold?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm a specialist in occupational health, then I specialised as a family doctor afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay, sir, now do you have any medical opinion as to whether in fact this bullet had been fired at close range or not?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the case of other dead people I think they were all shot from close range. In the case of the last person I think it was shot from some distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: When you say the last person, are we talking about Jetish Xhafa?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. He now lives well. He was almost twice buried alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, unfortunately I do have some more questions but I would be moving on to another area and I think we should stop now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You must know also, Mr. Ivetic, that there was hardly any foundation, in fact there is no foundation there for that opinion. So ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For what it's worth, I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You have, I think, a clear indication of the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we shall have to adjourn again, Dr. Gerxhaliu. We will resume again tomorrow at 2.15 and, at that stage, we will hopefully complete your evidence. I remind you again that it's important you do not discuss any aspect of your evidence with anyone before you return here tomorrow afternoon at 2.15. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I had requested if I could make a brief oral application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There is no time to do that, Mr. Hannis. I know what you want to do but it will have to wait until the end of this witness's evidence. Hopefully you've alerted the Defence to what the --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I have, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- position is and we can deal with it fairly quickly tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 31st day of August, 2006, at 2.15 p.m. 16 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.03 p.m.,
